global_production_rules.title: Authority and allocation
global_production_rules.text: Use this V07 panelized manuscript for the 105-page allocation taken from CH 01 PAGINATION PROPOSAL V02. The author’s instruction to proceed to panelisation is the basis for this pass. V06 page numbers are historical source locators only. They are not current page or panel IDs. No page has been moved, added or removed.

global_production_rules.title: Production identity
global_production_rules.text: PANEL ID format: CH01-P###-PN##. The three-digit P number is the graphic-novel page, and PN is the panel in reading order on that page. PN numbering restarts at 01 on each page. Always combine the ID with manuscript revision V07; an identically named V06 panel is not the same production assignment. Use V07/CH01-P###-PN## as the revision-qualified job key. Asset versions may add an ART or version suffix without changing panel identity.

global_production_rules.title: Panel versus layout
global_production_rules.text: A panel is a content/scene unit, not a compulsory decorative box. Panel types describe function, not geometry. The Page Layout Director chooses proportions, framing, typography and composition under Design Guide V04. Compatible teaching panels can share a visual enclosure while their IDs, complete content and reading order remain distinct. A new panel ID does not by itself require a new illustration.

global_production_rules.title: Content lock
global_production_rules.text: Preserve every source paragraph, dialogue line, complete question, calculation, answer, table, diagram and semantic emphasis. Keep each panel on its stated page and read panels in their numbered order. Do not rewrite, shorten, silently correct, reveal an unsupplied answer, merge incompatible story states, or import content from an older manuscript or a design sample. Panel focus lines and identifiers are non-printable metadata.

global_production_rules.title: Printable versus production text
global_production_rules.text: Only the source content under PRINTABLE CONTENT is learner-facing. All page/panel headers, source locators, reference filenames, direction notes are production metadata. Six standalone source labels “Narration” are retained in place under explicit NON-PRINTABLE — SOURCE ROLE LABEL markers; these label narration and are not story copy. Speaker names and prefixes remain in their exact source text, with speaker ownership also recorded in the manifest; do not silently strip source-owned printable prefixes.

global_production_rules.title: Reference selection
global_production_rules.text: Read the complete scene description first. Check the named reference against the required location, viewpoint and story stage. Preserve literal filenames, including supplied spelling and double extensions. If a name is outdated or mismatched, use a clearly matching current approved source only after identifying it, and record the selected filename and reason. Flag ambiguous matches instead of guessing. Do not substitute an explicitly locked approved image without author approval. Source exceptions and the current scene state still apply.

global_production_rules.title: Reference-review scope
global_production_rules.text: This pass checks the association between names, descriptions and panel content. The author will update older source images after panelisation. No asset is declared missing merely because an earlier archive is incomplete, and this pass does not certify availability, version selection, image sharpness or final artwork. Resolve the current actual images when creating prompts.

global_production_rules.title: Standalone panel handoff
global_production_rules.text: Read the page-common notes and then the complete assigned panel note. The opening’s three shared visual notes are retained once for traceability; each affected panel also has a resolved view-specific brief. Send only that resolved view and its own reference files to the image model, not all competing views in the shared note. The JSON manifest carries explicit common-note and assigned-note scope.

global_production_rules.title: Continuity
global_production_rules.text: Character sheets govern identity; the current scene governs pose, props, handedness, lighting and repair stage. Preserve the same location geography, prop ownership and cause-and-effect across cuts and page turns. Track faulty versus corrected controls, local indicator changes versus street lighting, and intact/missing/installed objects separately. A silent character feature is not a new story event. Keep required appearances and authored remarks; do not add characters as a quota.

global_production_rules.title: Exact maths and design
global_production_rules.text: Use the attached ChandRush Design Guide V04 for visual language and final-size requirements. Keep extended teaching on calm light surfaces. Image-generated diagram drafts may illustrate source-defined relationships, but final labels, notation, tables and mathematical evidence require exact checking and separable controlled construction. The manuscript does not allocate panel sizes, set new word budgets, or grant blanket permission for smaller type.

global_production_rules.title: Release boundary
global_production_rules.text: Panelisation and source-preservation checks are distinct from a tested automated page-creation run. Before production, resolve the two source diagram details listed below, select the updated source assets, and check the initial generated/assembled pages for full visible content, correct maths, identity, state and readable final placement. Do not regenerate unrelated correct work to fix one local issue.

content_blocks.text: ChandRush is a travelling full-moon fair that celebrates students' love of mathematics. Every year, ChandRush appears in a city somewhere in the world. For one night, students from that city come together to play, eat, explore and celebrate numbers, patterns, shapes, measurements and chance. ChandRush does not divide children into 'good at maths' and 'bad at maths'. It does not ask for report cards or marks. Every student is welcome. Some arrive because they already love mathematics; others arrive because they are curious and willing to try. The fair belongs to all of them.

Some arrive because they already love mathematics; others arrive because they are curious and willing to try. The fair belongs to all of them.

content_blocks.text: When something is mathematically wrong, ChandRush magic copies or exaggerates the mistake. Tez calls this Moon Mischief. A wrong number can make lights flash at the wrong time. A wrong fraction can make portions change size. A wrong shape can make part of a building behave as if the shape itself is confused.
